title: Habitats
standard_text: Identify the basic needs of plants and animals, including air, water, food or shelter, and describe how the places they live meet those needs (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 1 science worksheets on habitats: where plants and animals live in Australia, small habitats under logs, and how habitats give food, water and shelter. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A habitat gives plants and animals the food, water and shelter they need.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every living thing has a habitat.

  • Koalas live in gum trees.
  • Fish live in water.
  • Worms live in damp soil.
Example

Where does a platypus live?

it swims and digs

Answer: in creeks and rivers

Common mistakes

  • Thinking any animal can live anywhere.
  • Putting sea animals in a land habitat.

faq.a: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives. It gives the living thing what it needs.
A microhabitat is a very small habitat, such as under a log or a rock, where minibeasts live.
Australia has bushland, rainforests, deserts, wetlands, rivers, beaches and coral reefs.
